text:
sara-support: FYI — ACME reporting a spike of 503s hitting their hosted endpoints starting ~13:05 PT. They say calls fail mid-stream for long responses.
devon-sre: Seeing the same in prod metrics, p95 errors up. Gateway logs show upstream closed connection with status 0xFF, workers marked as unhealthy.
mike-eng-runtime: I pulled logs from the affected node pool (gpupool-17). There's a repeating pattern: inference process exits with "device reset" then container gets restarted by kubelet.
anya-ml: Any OOM messages in dmesg or driver logs? device reset could be a GPU reset from NVML or a cuda abort.
mike-eng-runtime: NVML shows: "GPU: 0: Reset detected" then later runtime log: "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'" not always, but also a few SIGSEGVs inside attention kernel. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T20:12:31Z] runtime: infer_worker[pid:2345] ERROR: CUDA error: device-side assert
[2026-03-17T20:12:31Z] runtime: infer_worker[pid:2345] FATAL: Received signal SIGSEGV at addr 0x7ff...
```
jordan-cs: Customer reported it happens more when they stream long outputs with many tool calls. Might be correlated with KV cache size + long sequences.
lisa-oncall: Are there recent deploys or quantization changes for model v2.3? Ops bot shows a canary swap earlier today.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout completed for model/redwood-v2-quantized @ 2026-03-17T19:40:12Z (trigger: auto-quant-suggest). No rollbacks.
mike-eng-runtime: Timeline: canary rollout -> small increase in GPU mem pressure -> after ~20m device resets begin on a subset of hosts -> cluster autoscaler restarts pods -> customer 503s.
devon-sre: Repro attempt on staging with same model + long stream: forced memory growth triggers cuda driver reset within 90s. Repro steps below.
anya-ml: Post them here and we can try mitigations (batching limits, disable kv prefetch, switch to float16 lazy allocation).
mike-eng-runtime: Repro steps (staging gpupool-stress):
1) Pull model redwood-v2-quantized:tag=2026-03-17
2) Send streaming request with context length 12k tokens and enable toolcall, kv_prefetch=true
3) Ramp QPS to 8 concurrent streams
Result: Within 60-120s worker process crashes with device reset and kernel SIGSEGV.
jordan-cs: Temporary mitigation for ACME: route them to dedicated fallback model (redwood-v2-std) and enable ``no-prefetch`` flag. CS on call can apply route override.
sara-support: Applied route override for ACME -> redwood-v2-std at 13:30 PT. Customer confirms reduced 503s but higher latency/cost.
lisa-oncall: For hotfix: can we pin canary back to previous quantization profile (rollback canary)? We should also add a guard in runtime to reject contexts > 8k tokens for quantized models.
mike-eng-runtime: I can push a quick rollback of the canary and a config that disables kv_prefetch for quantized profiles. Need a ±15m window to apply and observe.
devon-sre: I'll schedule the rollback and monitor nvml/drivers. Also adding more verbose kernel logs to capture kernel stack on crash.
anya-ml: We'll run a targeted eval with long-context prompts to verify quality regressions before/after rollback.
lisa-oncall: Postmortem owners: eng-runtime (mike), SRE (devon), ML (anya), CS (jordan), Support (sara). We'll treat as Sev-2 until root cause identified.
sara-support: Customer happy with fallback; keeping them updated. Will escalate billing questions if they're concerned about extra tokens during fallback.
mike-eng-runtime: Status update 13:55 PT — rollback started, canary aborted, nodes drained and restarted with previous model binary. Initial telemetry shows device resets stopped on gpupool-17.
devon-sre: Monitoring for next 60m, setting alert thresholds lower. Will follow up with logs + heap snapshot if we see recurrence.
jordan-cs: Noting CS next steps: confirm with ACME that errors ceased for 24h, offer credits if needed, and schedule a call for postmortem.
sara-support: Thanks team — looping in billing for potential credits. Marking thread for postmortem doc creation.
